description_ai_system_en: Fuzzy Search (SSAName3) is a critical software tool used by CBSA to flag high risk travellers and goods. Utilized to conduct fuzzy name searching and matching across a number of CBSA’s lines of business solutions (Travellers, Commercial and Intelligence & Enforcement), particularly mission critical systems. The software processes data across multiple different datasets so they are properly indexed, identified, scored and ranked.
Self-service option for travellers arriving at Canadian airports to complete Primary Processing while crossing the border.

Darktrace is a cybersecurity system that uses artificial intelligence (AI) to detect, investigate, and respond to cyber threats in real time. AI is used to learn normal patterns of behavior across networks, devices, and users, enabling the system to identify anomalies that may signal malicious activity. The business problem prompting AI use was the growing complexity, speed, and unpredictability of cyberattacks, which traditional rule-based security tools struggled to manage. The objective of the system is to provide autonomous threat detection and response, reducing reliance on manual intervention and minimizing the time to identify and contain threats.

Block 18 of the Record of Employment (ROE) is a text field for information about exceptional circumstances not captured elsewhere. However, Service Canada often receives ROEs with redundant or irrelevant information in block 18. The Record of Employment Comments Classification (ROECC) model processes comments in Block 18 to determine whether they contain information about the Reason for Separation and compare it with the RFS in Block 16.

Use of computer vision to help validate the authenticity of identity documents uploaded by clients, as well as, reading, comparing, and extracting data from them. 
These documents will be submitted online as scans and/or photos (e.g.*.jpeg, *.pdf, etc.).

Recalculation of Employment Insurance (EI) takes place when circumstances change or new information emerges that could make benefit calculations inaccurate. Where the initial benefit rate or weeks of entitlement were underestimated and EI underpaid, the claim is adjusted to compensate for the financial shortfall. In cases of overpayment, the claim is reduced to recover the excess amount. When no changes are identified and the initial benefit rate and weeks of entitlement were accurate, the claim remains unchanged. The primary objective of the EI Machine Learning Workload is to reduce the time spent by officers on claim reviews by identifying cases where a recalculation will not result in any change. This approach allows officers to focus on more complex reviews that require intervention and precision to ensure clients receive the correct benefit rate and entitlement.

description_ai_system_en: This project seeks to streamline the processing of privately sponsored refugee applications using automation technology to help IRCC officers process applications more efficiently.

The software, Dragon Naturally Speaking, is being used to fulfill accommodation requirements to assist an individual with a disability in the workplace. Specifically, this software offers speech-to-text and text-to-speech functionalities.

This project seeks to evaluate and mitigate the risk level of cargo inbound to Canada before it is loaded onto an aircraft, adding a layer of security to Canada’s Aviation network. It is used to review cargo manifest for inbound flights in order to identify potential risks to aviation security. https://tc.canada.ca/en/programs/pre-load-air-cargo-targeting-pact. Transport Canada incorporates an artificial intelligence solution into the Pre-load air cargo targeting uses artifical intelligence (specifically supervised machine learning and natural language processing) to interpret text, conduct identity resolution (related to shipper and consignee names and commodity descriptions), and to classify and group free-text data fields found in air cargo information for the purpose of risk assessing inbound shipments to Canada.

name_ai_system_en: Automation Development to Support Disability Benefit Decision Making
description_ai_system_en: The project is to increase VAC use of automation technologies to improve throughput of disability decisions and reduce the overall backlog. One component, Service Health Record Search Tool (SHRST) used an AI handwriting and text extraction function to  read handwritten and typed information within client files as part of extracting Service Health Record information related to disability claims for use in aiding decision making. This benefits the decision making process through saving many hours of manual processing of these files.  Another component uses the same AI technology to to read handwriting within Client Application files as part of automatically transcribing scanned paper applications for disability claims. Developed in part by the VAC  AI Development and Modernization Development teams.

The Security Screening Automation (SSA) Project is designed to expedite the review of security screening referrals. While the project seeks to automate many components of the triage function to support officers in their review of security screening referrals, the deployment of a Large Language Model is the only AI component being deployed within the project. Data, provided as part of the referral, is assessed against pre-defined areas of concern. These potential concerns are then identified to screening officers to support their review of the referral. The semantic capabilities of open-source large language models (LLM) are then used to create short narrative summaries to assist the screening officers. The LLM is asked to attempt and identify the existence of certain pre-determined areas of concerns.

Travellers Compliance Indicators (TCI) is a series of algorithms to assist border officers in identifying likely compliant travellers. It is currently in development and will not be in production before 2026.
Machine learning model developed in-house to assess the risk of outgoing export shipments.

CATSA is exploring the possibility of implementing a Human Resources Management System (HRMS) to manage position changes, track historical data, and enhance capabilities for Pay Equity, succession management, and recruitment. Leverage AI tools to streamline manual HR processes and automate tasks to improve efficiency.

CATSA is exploring the possibility of implementing a tool that will support improved search capabilities, alignment with business intelligence (BI) reporting, and automation of key  Complaints and Claims processes.

Environment and Climate Change Canada's Digital Services Branch built a correspondence monitoring tool to monitor and categorize Form Letter emails. Proof of Concept project to explore the automated management of a general delivery mailbox. An AI workflow is scheduled to look at the gd mailbox on a set schedule and read every new email, tag it with relevant information, determine if it is an email of business value, and remove/report emails that are not. Undesirable emails (SPAM,Phishing,form letters,...) are archived and metadata is captured. There is also a reporting capability for the GD mailbox owner to view through a dashboard the landscape of emails received across time.

name_ai_system_en: Passport Automated Decision-Making in IRCC’s Global Case Management System (GCMS)
description_ai_system_en: This project seeks to streamline processing of passport applications. This project seeks to examine how any identified unintended outcomes may be mitigated while supporting passport application processing and particularly how applicants are triaged by the system to streamline identity, eligibility, and entitlement determinations.

AAST is a processing aid to help staff complete administrative tasks for immigration applications, including data matching and bulk email creation. Biometric enrolments are completed by Visa Application Centres (VACs) and IRCC offices. The client is photographed and fingerprinted using Government of Canada software and hardware and basic biographic details are exported and entered into the Biometric Module in AAST. Immigration medical examinations are conducted by Panel Physicians who submit the information electronically to IRCC, which is then entered into the Medical Module in AAST.The Biometric and Medical modules of the AAST use index matching of lists of biographical information between the biometric enrolments and immgration medical examinations, and applications pending those assessments. This helps ensure that biometric enrollments and medical assessments are connected to immigration applications in a timely manner.

name_ai_system_en: Pro B AI Chatbot and Agent Interface
description_ai_system_en: A foundational tool allowing for interaction with one or more AI models, similar to CANChat and Radia in allowing interaction, agents, knowledge bases and limited tools to enable the organization to implement some of the other Use Cases listed under the ISC and CIRNAC desired projects. Initial phases will attempt to have a similar set of standard data sources to Radia Pro solution.  Future iterations may allow for intergrations with MS Graph for email, calendar and SharePoint integrations (when the department is ready for this).  Eliminating the need for MS 365 Copilot licences just for this functionality.  Internal Service related data will be the focus in initial phases as more risk assessments and engagment will be required before moving to more sensitive data use with AI tools.

name_ai_system_en: Transkribus Transcription: Canadian Newspapers Index & Order-in-Council Registers (1925 to 1940)
description_ai_system_en: Pilot transcription projects using Transkribus AI model to improve access to historical records: (1) Index of Canadian Newspapers and (2) Order-in-Council Registers (1925 to 1940). Both projects aim to digitize and transcribe records for improved access and digital storage. Developed by LAC in collaboration with READ-COOP (Transkribus, originating from EU-funded READ project, University of Innsbruck)

AI-powered enterprise chat platform for Public Safety Canada and Government of Canada employees. The system provides secure, bilingual (EN/FR) conversational AI access through a modern web interface with 30+ specialized agents covering domains such as cyber security, IT project costing, policy research, translation, and coding assistance. Users interact through individual AI chat or real-time collaborative Team Rooms with @PSChat AI mentions. The platform supports multi-format document upload and analysis (PDF, Word, Excel, images), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) via vector search over indexed knowledge bases, and exportable reports (PDF, Word, Markdown). An Agent Marketplace allows creation, submission, review, and deployment of custom AI agents. An admin dashboard provides usage analytics, cost tracking, and rate-limit monitoring.
